title: NSUI stages protest against hazardous air pollution in Delhi, demands immediate action

ai.summary: The National Students’ Union of India staged a protest in Delhi demanding immediate action to address hazardous air pollution, citing health risks for citizens.

facts.claim: The National Students’ Union of India staged a protest against hazardous air pollution in the national capital on Thursday
facts.quote: The National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) staged a protest against hazardous air pollution in the national capital on Thursday, demanding immediate government intervention to tackle the worsening situation and protect public health.

facts.claim: Students and activists gathered at the organisation’s headquarters on Raisina Road and took out a protest march
facts.quote: Led by NSUI national president Vinod Jakhar, students and activists gathered at the organisation’s headquarters on Raisina Road and took out a protest march, raising concerns over the deteriorating pollution levels and their impact on residents.

facts.claim: Delhi’s polluted air had put the health and daily lives of ordinary citizens at serious risk, with children and older adults particularly vulnerable
facts.quote: Addressing the protesters, Jakhar said Delhi’s polluted air had put the health and daily lives of ordinary citizens at serious risk, with children and older adults particularly vulnerable.

facts.claim: The government and responsible agencies have failed to deliver concrete solutions
facts.quote: Despite repeated warnings and the worsening situation, the government and responsible agencies have failed to deliver concrete solutions.

facts.claim: Students demand clean air for a healthy Delhi
facts.quote: NSUI members and students held oxygen masks to their noses and held up placards saying "students demand clean air for a healthy Delhi".

ai.background_note: The protest is part of ongoing efforts to address Delhi's air pollution crisis, with the NSUI demanding immediate government action.
